title: Multidimensional arrays and row/column traversal
learningObjectives: Declare and initialize two-dimensional arrays as arrays of row arrays.
Use row and column indices within their separate bounds.
Traverse two-dimensional arrays with nested loops.
Explain row-major storage order and contiguous rows.
Pass multidimensional arrays to functions with the required column bound.

understand.concept: A two-dimensional array in C is an array whose elements are themselves arrays. For `int grid[2][3]`, the outer array has two rows and each row has three int elements. The valid row indices are 0–1 and column indices 0–2. C stores the elements in row-major order, with each row's elements contiguous.
understand.whyItMatters: This concept supports correct handling of C data and helps prevent invalid memory access or incorrect program behaviour.
understand.analogy: Think of the construct as a precisely bounded sequence of storage and operations.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's rules for object lifetime, bounds, types or undefined behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Declare a two-dimensional array

`int grid[2][3]` defines two rows, each containing three integers. It is not a special matrix object; it is an array of two elements whose element type is an array of three int values.

## 2. Initialize rows

Use nested braces such as `{{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}}`. The first subscript selects the row and the second selects the column. Both bounds must be respected.

## 3. Traverse with nested loops

The outer loop commonly visits rows and the inner loop visits columns. Use the actual row and column counts to set the loop limits. A swapped bound can read outside a row or skip data.

## 4. Row-major storage

C stores each row's elements contiguously, then the next row. This matters when reasoning about pointer arithmetic, memory layout and performance. The array's element type is an array, so pointer arithmetic follows the row type at the outer level.

## 5. Function parameters

When passing a two-dimensional array to a function, the compiler must know the size of each row to calculate element addresses. A parameter can be written with a fixed column bound or a variable-length array bound where supported by the selected C version. Pass the row count separately when it is needed.

questions.prompt: How many int elements are in `int a[2][3]`?
questions.explanation: There are two rows with three elements each.
The first subscript selects the row and the second selects the column.

options: All elements of one row are stored contiguously before the next row
Columns are stored as separate linked lists
Each element is stored at a random address
questions.answer: All elements of one row are stored contiguously before the next row
questions.explanation: C arrays store nested row arrays contiguously.

questions.prompt: Why does a function parameter for a 2D array need the column bound?
options: The compiler needs the row type size to calculate element addresses
It is required only for printing
The column count is stored in the function name
questions.answer: The compiler needs the row type size to calculate element addresses
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic across rows depends on the size of each row.

questions.prompt: Which traversal pattern visits every element of a 2 by 3 array?
options: Two nested loops with row limit 2 and column limit 3
One loop with index less than 2 only
One loop with index less than 3 only
questions.answer: Two nested loops with row limit 2 and column limit 3
questions.explanation: Each dimension needs its own valid index range.
